setKeyNote: This manifest's setKey is the BARE PRODUCT key ('donruss', pre-2009 spelling per DONRUSS_SPELLING_POLICY/PANINI_DONRUSS_FROM_YEAR=2009 in productSetKeys.ts, already registered P("donruss", { family: "donruss" }) at ~line 1049) fed to ingest-checklist-csv-to-catalog.cjs as productOf()'s product.setKey, exactly mirroring the sibling acq-2026-09-20-cardboardconnection-donruss-1985 package's manifest. Every row's own category='insert-the-rookies' is what actually derives this insert set's OWN card-set key at ingest time -- see setKeyNeedsRuling below for why that derived key is not yet usable.
setKeyRulingNote: PROPOSED, not registered as its own P()/S() entry in productSetKeys.ts. productSetKeys.ts registers the bare setKey literal 'the-rookies' ONLY under two Panini-era (2009+) families -- 'donruss-optic-the-rookies' (family donruss-optic, ~line 1179) and 'panini-donruss-the-rookies' (family panini-donruss, ~line 1922) -- both modern insert sets of the current Panini Donruss/Donruss Optic products, unrelated to this 1987 vintage boxed set. Panini acquired Donruss in 2009 (PANINI_DONRUSS_FROM_YEAR = 2009; DONRUSS_SPELLING_POLICY = 'panini-era', productSetKeys.ts lines 62-71); the bare pre-2009 'donruss' product IS already registered as a plain product (P("donruss", { family: "donruss" }), line 1049). There is currently no registered setKey for a vintage/bare 'Donruss The Rookies' 1987 boxed set as its own product. MEASURED directly against this branch's planStagedDirectory (real ingest lane, read-only, no Cosmos), run twice: (1) this file ALONE -- verdict 'pass', separate=[] (nothing to separate against in an empty cell), every row lands on the BARE 'donruss' key, i.e. the SAME address as the flagship's own #1-55 base rows; (2) this file staged ALONGSIDE the already-committed flagship package (acq-2026-09-13-bcp/1987-donruss-baseball.csv) in one directory -- verdict 'pass' for BOTH files, separate=['the-rookies'] correctly measured cross-file (subsetsToSeparate/separationByCell do see the cross-file clash e.g. at #14: this set's Bo Jackson vs the flagship's Kevin McReynolds DK, both otherwise hiq:baseball:1987:donruss:14:base:no-auto), and the Rookies rows ARE separated onto 'donruss-the-rookies' -- but the file still PASSES rather than refusing for an unregistered key, because unregisteredKeys' test is `normalizeSetKey(k) !== k`, and normalizeSetKey('donruss-the-rookies') returns 'donruss-the-rookies' unchanged (falls through every rewrite rule to a no-op slugify) -- IDEMPOTENT UNDER NORMALIZATION IS NOT THE SAME THING AS REGISTERED, and this key is idempotent-but-unregistered, a blind spot in the mechanical guard for exactly this shape (a proposed key that already happens to be well-formed slug text). CONCLUSION: the automated collision guard is NOT a safety net here -- ingesting this file today, whether alone or beside the flagship, would silently write real rows, and if done beside the flagship in the same run it would write them to an unregistered, unreviewed key ('donruss-the-rookies') that nothing else in the matcher/pricing path is guaranteed to resolve correctly. A human ruling is needed BEFORE any ingest of this file for this reason, not because the tooling will refuse it. TWO OPTIONS proposed, not decided here: (1) register 'donruss-the-rookies' as its own S() entry under the bare 'donruss' product family (parallels how 'donruss-elite' and 'donruss-studio' are registered as their own P() products alongside bare 'donruss'), or (2) register 'donruss-rookies-1987' as a standalone boxed-set product with no family relation to flagship Donruss, since 'The Rookies' was sold as its own dealer-only boxed factory set, not a pack-inserted subset of the 660-card flagship, and giving it a wholly separate product key sidesteps any cross-set numbering ambiguity by construction. Do not register either key and do not run APPLY ingest without Drew's ruling.
readyToIngestNote: Blocked on the setKeyNeedsRuling gate above. Measured (see setKeyRulingNote): planStagedDirectory PASSES this file today, both alone and alongside the already-staged flagship package, so the mechanical ingest guard will NOT refuse it -- the block is a human ruling, not a tooling gate. Do not run ingest-checklist-csv-to-catalog.cjs with APPLY=true / BACKFILL_APPLY=true against this directory (or any directory containing it) until productSetKeys.ts registers a fixed-point key for the 1987 boxed set per one of the two proposed options in setKeyRulingNote. Separately, this directory sits under backend/data/checklists/scraped/ where a human/workflow chooses which directories to point DIR at -- staging alone never triggers a write.
gapThisFills: 2026-09-28 acquisition queue, one of four Drew ordered same day. Gap analysis found 21,882 unbacked sales at cell 1987|panini-donruss (label: 'Donruss box-set insert (Rookies) distinct from flagship; base flagship also unapplied'). This package covers ONLY the 56-card 'The Rookies' boxed insert set -- it does NOT touch the 660-card 1987 Donruss base/flagship set, which is a separate, already-staged product elsewhere in the acquisition pipeline. Because the setKey this insert needs is unregistered (see setKeyRulingNote), none of the 21,882 unbacked sales are unlocked by this PR alone; this package only stages the checklist so the sales can be matched once the ruling lands and a follow-on ingest runs.
sourcePageShape: Baseball Almanac's one-set checklist page (baseball_cards_oneset.php?s=1987don02) lists a bare 'NUMBER. Player Name' line per card, #1-56, with #56 printed as 'Checklist' (the set's own numbered checklist card, not a player). Cross-checked in full against BaseballCardPedia's 1987 Donruss The Rookies article (same 56 rows, XRC annotations for extended-rookie-card players, #56 also listed as the checklist card) and Wax Pack Gods' set guide (same 56 rows and note). All three sources agree on every row; minor spelling variants across sources (e.g. Ken Williams/Kenny Williams, Mike Jackson/Michael Jackson, Bill Ripken/Billy Ripken, James Steels/Jim Steels) were resolved to BaseballCardPedia's spelling as this package's primary transcription source, cross-referenced against Baseball Almanac.
converterNote: Rows transcribed by hand from the fetched checklist text (no HTML scraper script needed for a 56-row page): number and player name copied verbatim per source, category stamped 'insert-the-rookies' uniformly (no base tier exists in this file -- see heldOut), isAuto=false and printRun blank for every row (no source states either), parallel left blank (no named parallel is claimed by any of the three sources for this set).

sectionsReport.note: OWN numbering for the entire boxed set, 1-55 (see heldOut for #56). This is a standalone dealer-only factory set distributed in its own small green-and-black box, never packed with or numbered against the 660-card 1987 Donruss flagship, and its numbers DO overlap the flagship's own 1-660 range (this set's #14 is Bo Jackson; the flagship's #14 is Kevin McReynolds DK -- confirmed by reading acq-2026-09-13-bcp/1987-donruss-baseball.csv on this branch). See setKeyRulingNote for the measured cross-file address clash this causes on the bare 'donruss' key and why it needs a registered key, not just a category name, to resolve safely.

heldOut.reason: Not a player card -- all three sources list #56 as the checklist card itself, the same shape as the 1985 Donruss sibling package's excluded 'NNO Diamond Kings Checklist' filler cards. No player name to key an identity on. Held out rather than staged as e.g. player='Checklist', per the same exclusion rule as that sibling package.

relatedProductNote: The 660-card 1987 Donruss base/flagship set is a SEPARATE product, already staged elsewhere in the acquisition pipeline (acq-2026-09-13-bcp/1987-donruss-baseball.csv, manifest setKey 'donruss'), and this PR does NOT touch, modify, or merge into that file or its rows. This package's own category ('insert-the-rookies') is distinct from the flagship's ('base'), but the two sets DO share card-number values (both run roughly 1-55/56 and 1-660 respectively, so e.g. #14 exists in both) -- see setKeyRulingNote for why that overlap needs a registered setKey to resolve to two distinct addresses rather than one shared, colliding address on bare 'donruss'.
